@{5d60e4d6698f8c20c0f5a295|full_name}: Bit of a weird subject because one could make the argument that eye tracking on VR headset's would jump as soon as VR games (especially ones that are hard to run) implement Foveated rendering. As soon as one or two companies add eye tracking + Foveated Rendering capabilities to their headset and have a decent amount of games support it, all of a sudden other companies would be forced to do the same as those headsets with eye tracking and Foveated rendering would have a substantial performance increase and GPU load decrease compared to headsets that didn't use Foveated Rendering.
In CES 2020 Pimax showed a full on Foveated rendering demo to participants and they could barely notice it except for a bit of low resolution around the edges of their view but as the tech get's refined it would be nearly impossible to notice. 
Facebook (Oculus) has been looking into Foveated Rendering and showed pretty good progress in 2019.
And Nvidia looked into Foveated Rendering for VR all the way back in 2016.
Hopefully the Quest 2 has eye tracking capabilities and if so I don't think the main purpose of it will be to utilize eye tracking in-games like VRChat, that's just a bonus. It's main purpose would likely be for Foveated rendering to drastically increase it's performance as the Oculus Quest (1) already has this in the form of Fixed Foveated Rendering or the type you can notice. If not the Quest 2 would also likely use FFR.
https://developer.oculus.com/documentation/native/android/mobile-ffr/?device=QUEST

If this was any other game i wouldn't have seen any meaning to eye tracking, but it being a social game the eye tracking would add a new level of expression similarly to full body tracking. NeosVR and VirtualCast already support this so i don't really think it's that hard to implement at this point.

Blinking can be controlled without bones if they write the code for it. It can be done by mapping the raw data from the eye tracker to a blendshape on the avatar (for example, mapping the raw eye closed values to the blinking blendshapes). This can easily be done very quickly, so it would allow any avatar to work flawlessly with it.
